Getting started with scphasedcn

Source: vignettes/scphasedcn.Rmd
scphasedcn.Rmd

scphasedcn calls copy-number alterations in single cells from SPLONGGET data: single-cell long-read DNA sequencing in which every read carries a 10x Multiome cell barcode and is sequenced on Oxford Nanopore. Per cell and region it combines two channels:

  • depth: fragments per region against an expected count from a reference (cells of the same cell type in normal tissue, a GC / mappability model in tumours), scored as a z against a Student-t null;
  • read-phased alleles: every molecule that covers a phased heterozygous SNP votes for one haplotype; allelic imbalance is scored with beta-binomial likelihood ratios.

Two modes:

  • normal tissue (mode = "normal"): rare, cell-private events. Thresholds come from null cells (cells the caller selects as copy-number neutral, or that you give), cross-validated at 1 false call per 1,000 null cell-regions; cells are also called in pools (random pools within a cell type, chromatin-kNN pools). Named events (events) are called per cell; their pooled calls are off by default (pool_events: experimental, not calibrated per event).
  • tumour (mode = "tumour"): clones. The caller discovers clones, fits their allele-specific copy-number states, re-assigns every cell by likelihood and reports per-cell calls inherited from the clone or confirmed by the cell.

The workflow

  1. Phase heterozygous SNPs of the sample (e.g. Clair3 + longphase on the pooled BAM) and select them with scphasedcn select-hets.
  2. Extract with the Python package scphasedcn (scphasedcn run): per-cell 100 kb bin counts, a fragment table with the haplotype of every fragment, and per-cell QC.
  3. Call with call_scn() in R, or the command-line script shipped with the package.

vignette("scphasedcn-inputs") describes steps 1 and 2, the input files and the cell metadata; vignette("scphasedcn-outputs") the result tables.

A run on simulated data

The package simulates SPLONGGET-like data and writes it in the layout the extractor produces. Here: 120 cells of normal tissue (female) in three cell types, a few cells carrying private events (a chr1p loss, a chr8 gain), and one phase block per chromosome.

library(scphasedcn)
library(data.table)
#> 
#> Attaching package: 'data.table'
#> The following object is masked from 'package:base':
#> 
#>     %notin%
ev = data.table(chrom = c("chr1", "chr8"), start = c(0, 0), end = c(24e6, NA),
                cnA = c(1L, 2L), cnB = c(0L, 1L), type = "private")
sim = simulate_scn(n_cells = 120, sex = "female", cell_types = c(epi = 0.4, fib = 0.35, imm = 0.25),
                   depth = c(meanlog = log(15000), sdlog = 0.3), events = ev, private_frac = 0.08,
                   multiplet_rate = 0, phase_block_mean = 1e9, switch_rate = 2e-6, seed = 7)
dir = file.path(tempdir(), "extract")
invisible(write_sim_dataset(sim, dir))
list.files(dir)
#> [1] "alleles_dna.h5ad"     "bins_100kb.h5ad"      "cells_qc.tsv"        
#> [4] "fragments.tsv.gz"     "fragments.tsv.gz.tbi" "truth_cells.tsv"

The simulated genome is small (chr1, chr2, chr8, chr21, chr22, chrX), so the run gets a centromere table for it; on real hg38 data the default (hg38_centromeres()) applies.

cen = sim$scn$bins[, .(cstart = 1, len = max(end)), by = chrom]
cen = cen[, .(chrom, cstart, cen_left = 0.4 * len, cen_right = 0.4 * len, cend = len)]

The cell types are in the simulated cells_qc.tsv; on real data they come from your own annotation through make_cell_meta().

res = call_scn(dir, mode = "normal", sex = "female", centromeres = cen, null_cells = "select", verbose = FALSE)
res
#> <scphasedcn> mode: normal
#>   cells: 120
#>   regions: 97
#>   calls: 13446 rows, 746 called, 653 reportable
#>   clones: 0
#>   notes: 14

Calls are per cell and region; events merges a cell’s overlapping calls into events.

head(res$events[, .(cell, chrom, start, end, state, top_region, score)])
#>         cell  chrom start     end  state top_region     score
#>       <char> <char> <num>   <num> <char>     <char>     <num>
#> 1: cell_0002   chr1     0 2.4e+07   loss      chr1p 144.56874
#> 2: cell_0010   chr1     0 2.4e+07   loss      chr1p 131.50942
#> 3: cell_0018   chr1     0 2.4e+07   loss      chr1p 140.64205
#> 4: cell_0030   chr8     0 3.0e+07   gain       chr8  61.25552
#> 5: cell_0042   chr8     0 3.0e+07   gain       chr8  25.00741
#> 6: cell_0044   chr8     0 3.0e+07   gain       chr8  38.90160

Compare with the truth of the simulation (the cells carrying the chr1p loss):

carriers = colMeans(sim$truth$cn[sim$scn$bins$chrom == "chr1" & sim$scn$bins$end <= 24e6, ]) < 1.5
called = unique(res$events[chrom == "chr1" & state == "loss", cell])
table(carrier = sim$scn$cells$cell %in% sim$scn$cells$cell[carriers], called = sim$scn$cells$cell %in% called)
#>        called
#> carrier FALSE TRUE
#>   FALSE   104    0
#>   TRUE      0   16

Write all tables, the parameters and the run notes:

out = file.path(tempdir(), "caller")
invisible(write_scphasedcn(res, out))
list.files(out)
#>  [1] "calls.tsv"        "cells.tsv"        "events.tsv"       "false_calls.tsv" 
#>  [5] "false_events.tsv" "NOTES.md"         "null_fit.tsv"     "params.yaml"

From the command line

The package ships a command-line front end; its path is

system.file("scripts", "call_scn.R", package = "scphasedcn")
#> [1] "/home/runner/work/_temp/Library/scphasedcn/scripts/call_scn.R"
CALL=$(Rscript -e 'cat(system.file("scripts", "call_scn.R", package = "scphasedcn"))')
Rscript $CALL --dir results/sample/extract --out results/sample/caller --sex female --mode normal \
    --cell-meta cell_meta.tsv --null-cells select
Rscript $CALL --dir results/tumour/extract --out results/tumour/caller --sex male --mode tumour \
    --events "20q_gain=chr20:28000000-;3p_loss=chr3:1-90000000"
Rscript $CALL --help

Parameters

caller_params() reads the parameter file shipped with the package (inst/config/caller.yaml, one key per caller_defaults() entry plus normal: / tumour: blocks). To change a value, copy the file, edit it and pass it with --caller-config (or caller_params(file = ...) in R). Every run writes the values it used to params.yaml, which reads back with caller_params().

p = caller_params()
p[c("null_q", "eps", "mol_gap", "strata_breaks")]
#> $null_q
#> [1] 0.999
#> 
#> $eps
#> [1] 0.02
#> 
#> $mol_gap
#> [1] 2000
#> 
#> $strata_breaks
#> [1] 20000 50000

The defaults were calibrated on SPLONGGET normal-tissue and tumour samples: the one-copy depth shifts (shifts) on depth-only spike-ins into normal cells, null_q at 1 false call per 1,000 null cell-regions. The depth strata (strata_breaks, clean fragments per cell) separate cells whose power differs; with much deeper or shallower data, move them.

Tumour mode

Tumour mode needs read-phased alleles (the allele votes drive the clone discovery). Phase blocks of longphase are not oriented between blocks; the caller orients them per clone. Optional inputs: cells known to be normal (flat in the cell metadata: they set the input depth and allelic null; the reference pool is always the normal clone the caller finds), groups for the block orientation (groups, e.g. spatial regions), known events (events, reported as their own regions) and multiplet probabilities (multiplets).

res_t = call_scn("results/tumour/extract", mode = "tumour", sex = "male",
                 events = c(`20q_gain` = "chr20:28000000-"))
res_t$clones
head(res_t$segments)

MEDICC2 trees of the clones: medicc2_pieces() cuts the clone segments into common pieces, orient_clone_states() assigns each clone’s allele-specific copy numbers (cn_a, cn_b) from the molecule votes of the features, and medicc2_table() makes MEDICC2’s input table (write it yourself):

feat = cell_features("results/tumour/extract", method = "model", sex = "male")
res_t = call_scn("results/tumour/extract", mode = "tumour", features = feat)
pcs = medicc2_pieces(res_t$segments, res_t$clones)
ori = orient_clone_states(pcs, feat, res_t$assignments, res_t$clones)
data.table::fwrite(medicc2_table(ori), "medicc2_input.tsv", sep = "\t")
